families.name: Price and volume
families.lag: None — the close is the close
families.detail: Momentum, volatility, illiquidity, beta and idiosyncratic risk, all causal by construction.

families.name: SEC fundamentals
families.detail: Growth, margins, accruals, dilution. A fact may be used on a date only if it was public then.

families.name: Macro
families.source: FRED, plus the FOMC and election calendars
families.lag: Same-day for market data; calendars are known years ahead
families.detail: Rates, credit spreads, volatility, commodities, and proximity to policy and political events.

families.name: Institutional ownership
families.detail: Managers arriving and leaving, and whether the same crowd is building bigger positions.

families.name: Insider transactions
families.lag: Two business days, carried in the filing
families.detail: Open-market purchases and sales only. Grants and tax withholding are compensation, not decisions.

families.name: Earnings language
families.lag: None — the filing IS the announcement
families.detail: Tone, hedging and guidance, each measured as a change against the same company’s last release.

rejected.name: Concentration
rejected.claim: A high-conviction book of ten to fifteen names should beat a diversified one.
rejected.verdict: Rejected — it loses to the index outright.
rejected.why: At an information coefficient near 0.019 the top eight names are not reliably the best eight — they are the eight with the highest scores, which at that IC is mostly noise. A thin edge needs breadth.

rejected.name: Gârleanu-Pedersen trading
rejected.claim: The optimal policy under decaying alpha replaces the no-trade band.
rejected.verdict: Rejected — it buys 0.02 of Sharpe and costs 0.20 of return per unit of drawdown.
rejected.why: Turnover fell by up to 64%, which is what it was chosen for. Turnover was not the binding constraint, and the sweep is what showed that rather than an argument.

rejected.name: Confidence sizing
rejected.claim: Trade smaller when the model has recently been unreliable.
rejected.verdict: Rejected — 0.9 points of drawdown for 2.4 points of return.
rejected.why: The conformal interval is widest in violent markets, and those were the strongest months in the sample. The width measures volatility rather than unreliability, so the policy sizes down into the recovery.

rejected.name: Full covariance
rejected.claim: Portfolio optimisation and risk parity need the whole matrix.
rejected.verdict: Unusable at this sample size — roughly half of it is noise.
rejected.why: Marchenko-Pastur gives the band inside which eigenvalues are indistinguishable from noise. Six of a hundred directions carry 43% of the variance; the other ninety-four are random. The book uses only the diagonal, which was a simplification and turns out to have been right.

confirmed.name: Horizon matching
confirmed.claim: The holding period should match the label the model was trained on.
confirmed.detail: Monthly wins at Sharpe 1.0109 and is the only cadence that beats SPY. Not "slower is better" — quarterly is the worst of five. It is specifically 21 days.

confirmed.name: Survivorship, measured
confirmed.claim: Using today’s index membership for all history flatters the result.
confirmed.detail: Membership recovered from 110 snapshots back to 2012. IC falls from +0.02142 to +0.01851 once names are scored only on days they were actually in the index. It cost 87% of the excess RETURN, because a portfolio compounds what an average washes out.

guards.name: 13F availability
guards.tests: Every feature change lands on a statutory deadline
guards.sabotage: Lag set to zero: fails on 53 periods

guards.name: Form 4 windows
guards.tests: A rolling count moves only when a filing arrives or ages out

guards.name: Earnings language
guards.tests: A feature moves only on a filing date

guards.name: Conformal coverage
guards.tests: A 90% interval contains the outcome 90% of the time

guards.name: Marchenko-Pastur
guards.tests: Pure noise produces no eigenvalue above the band
guards.sabotage: Validated against theory before the real spectrum was read
